intro: Lesson 28. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: كَلَّا بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ (٢٠) وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ (٢١) وُجُوهٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ نَّاضِرَةٌ (٢٢) إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌۭ (٢٣) وَوُجُوهٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍۭ بَاسِرَةٌۭ (٢٤) تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌۭ (٢٥) كَلَّآ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلتَّرَاقِىَ (٢٦) وَقِيلَ مَنْ ۜ رَاقٍۢ (٢٧) وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ ٱلْفِرَاقُ (٢٨) وَٱلْتَفَّتِ ٱلسَّاقُ بِٱلسَّاقِ (٢٩) إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمَسَاقُ (٣٠)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: No! But you love the immediate And leave the Hereafter.
[Some] faces, that Day, will be radiant, Looking at their Lord.
And [some] faces, that Day, will be contorted, Expecting that there will be done to them [something] backbreaking.
No! When the soul has reached the collar bones And it is said, "Who will cure [him]?"
And the dying one is certain that it is the [time of] separation And the leg is wound about the leg,
To your Lord, that Day, will be the procession.

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Qiyamah 75:20-30 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 75:20-30 together without the mushaf.
saktah: a short pause with no breath
options: saktah: a short pause with no breath

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 75:20-30 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
Radiant faces looking at their Lord versus contorted faces expecting disaster.

questions.q: Why is the saktah needed in 75:27?
questions.a: Without it the noon would merge into the raa (idgham), and «مَن رَّاقٍ» could sound like one word.

questions.q: What will the radiant faces be doing (75:23)?
questions.a: A) Looking at their Lord. 75:23: 'Looking at their Lord.'

questions.q: Think again: 'But you love the immediate and leave the Hereafter' (75:20 to 21). Give an example from teenage life.
questions.a: Staying up on a phone instead of sleeping for Fajr; a quick reward now over a lasting one later.
